findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Changing RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 silently rewrites the public exit-code contract of `kc.sh update-compatibility check` in the same release that introduces exit code 4 with a completely different meaning (FEATURE_DISABLED). Any existing automation, CI pipeline, or wrapper script coded against the current constant (4 = recreate required) now receives 3 for recreate, and would interpret a future 4 (feature disabled) as 'recreate upgrade required' — the same numeric value now means the opposite thing depending on Keycloak version, with no deprecation or version note in the docs diff.

[ADVISORY] testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message and never asserts the FEATURE_DISABLED (4) exit code that UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() sets via picocli.exit(). A regression in the exit path (e.g. exit code returning 1/software error, or picocli.exit being skipped) passes the test suite while breaking every script and operator integration that branches on the documented exit code — which is the actual contract this diff adds.

[ADVISORY] The template hardcodes `--features=rolling-updates` onto the `update-compatibility` invocation in every rendered guide, including the upgrade path where a user runs the command against an existing older-versioned distribution. Users following the rendered doc while running `update-compatibility` against a Keycloak build where this feature enum value does not yet exist get an 'Unrecognized option / unknown feature' failure instead of the compatibility answer they were seeking; the flag also becomes permanently wrong once the feature is promoted past preview and the caution is removed.

[ADVISORY] The caution claims 'the {project_name} Operator will fail' when the feature is disabled, but this diff contains no operator production change that gates the update machinery on the ROLLING_UPDATES feature — the only enforcement added is in the two quarkus CLI commands. Operators who disable the feature and apply the documented CR see no operator failure (the reconciler path never checks the feature), leaving the doc asserting behavior the shipped code does not exhibit and masking whatever the intended failure mode was.

[ADVISORY] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently changed from 4 to 3, breaking any external script or CI job that branched on the old value 4 for 'recreate required'. Automation written against the previous binary (e.g. `if [ $? -eq 4 ]` in an upgrade pipeline) now falls through to its error/default branch when a recreate upgrade is required, without any error being raised; the diff contains no release-note or migration entry covering the changed contract.

[ADVISORY] testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message and never asserts the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4), so the new exit-code contract is unverified. A regression that returns the generic picocli usage/software exit code (1 or 2) instead of 4 would pass the test suite while silently breaking scripts that gate on exit code 4 to detect the disabled-feature case.

[ADVISORY] The documentation claims 'Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail', but the diff contains zero operator main-code changes that gate the update strategies on the rolling-updates feature, and no test exercises the operator without the feature enabled. An operator user who sets spec.update.strategy without enabling the feature gets whatever behavior the unchanged operator code already had (potentially a partially working or silently degraded rolling upgrade instead of the documented failure), and the UpgradeTest changes only cover the feature-enabled path, so the documented failure mode is completely unverified.

[ADVISORY] The new exit-code table row 4 ('Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature rolling-updates is disabled.') labels exit code 4 as an upgrade-possibility outcome, but the code treats it as a command-unusable error emitted before any compatibility evaluation, and no test or doc distinguishes these semantics. Users scripting against the documented table will conflate 'feature disabled' with a compatibility verdict, e.g. treating a misconfigured invocation (missing --features flag) as a legitimate 'recreate required' assessment of their deployment.

[BUG] The PR silently renumbers the public constant RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 to make room for FEATURE_DISABLED = 4, changing the documented contract of an already-released exit code. Any external automation (CI pipelines, upgrade scripts, the operator itself) that branched on exit code 4 meaning 'recreate upgrade required' now receives 3 and treats it as an unknown/software-error condition; the docs table in update-compatibility.adoc renumbered meaning of row '4' from recreate to feature-disabled, so existing consumers get silently wrong behavior with no migration note outside this diff.

[BUG] The docs claim the Operator will fail when `rolling-updates` is not enabled, but the diff contains zero operator-side code that checks the feature or produces that failure — the only enforcement added is in the two CLI commands. Operators following the documented behavior will find the Operator does not actually fail or gate anything on the feature; the stated invariant ('Operator fails without the feature') is not enforced anywhere in this diff, so a Keycloak CR with update.strategy set but no feature enabled proceeds with whatever the default behavior is, diverging from the documented contract.

[ADVISORY] The operator's custom test image now hard-codes --features=rolling-updates into the build, baking a preview feature into the shipped/tested operator image configuration rather than deriving it from the Keycloak CR's feature spec. The test suite tests the operator against a configuration users cannot reproduce through the CR alone (they must hand-build an image with the feature), so UpgradeTest passes while a user following only the documented CR fields (features.enabled) can still hit a non-matching image; also every future feature the operator's tests need will be appended to this Dockerfile string, a parallel hand-maintained list.

[BUG] FEATURE_DISABLED=4 silently repurposes the exit code that previously meant RECREATE_UPGRADE_REQUIRED (old constant was 4), while RECREATE moves to 3, so any external automation written against the old contract (shell scripts, CI pipelines, or a released operator version parsing literal exit codes) now interprets 'feature disabled' as 'recreate upgrade required' and vice versa. An existing script that ran `kc.sh update-compatibility ... ` and branched on exit code 4 to decide 'stop the deployment before upgrading' now takes that branch when the real condition is 'rolling-updates feature not enabled' — a completely different remediation (enable a feature flag vs. full downtime), and a genuine recreate-required result exits 3, which old callers treat as an unknown/software error. This is a cross-process contract broken with no version negotiation, exactly the skew a rolling-updates tool is supposed to survive.

[ADVISORY] The diff enables the rolling-updates feature in the operator's integration test setup and custom-image Dockerfile but adds no operator production code that propagates `--features=rolling-updates` into the managed StatefulSet pods or that fails reconciliation when the feature is absent, despite the docs claiming 'the Operator will fail'. Operators following the documented CR without the new `spec.features.enabled` entry get behavior that depends on enforcement living outside this diff (the server-side update-compatibility exit code 4); if the operator's reconciliation loop doesn't map exit 4 to a hard failure, the documented CAUTION is unenforced and a rolling upgrade proceeds against a server that can't validate compatibility. The enforcement path should exist and be exercised in the operator code/tests in this same change, not asserted only via docs.

[ADVISORY] The doc template appends `--features=rolling-updates` to every rendered `update-compatibility` invocation, including examples where the user is checking whether an existing deployment supports a rolling upgrade — which is precisely the case where the feature may not be enabled yet. A user upgrading from a deployment without the feature follows the doc example verbatim, runs the check with the flag, and gets the feature-disabled error (exit 4) from the same guide that told them to add the flag — the guide gives no instruction on how to enable a preview feature on an already-built server, dead-ending the documented workflow.

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was silently renumbered from 4 to 3 to make room for FEATURE_DISABLED=4, changing the CLI contract that existing automation depends on. Any script or CI pipeline written against the documented behavior that checks exit code 4 for 'recreate upgrade required' now sees 3 (interpreted as 'OK/rolling' territory by older consumers or simply unexpected) and, worse, a disabled-feature run returns 4 which those scripts will classify as 'recreate upgrade required' — an operator could shut down a production deployment based on a feature-flag error. This is a public exit-code surface changed without migration notes or acceptance, and the diff's own docs table only adds a new row for 4 without acknowledging that 4 previously meant recreate.

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently changed from 4 to 3, breaking any external automation/scripting that branches on exit code 4 for recreate-required, and no test in the diff asserts the recreate exit code at all. A CI pipeline or operator script written against the documented exit code 4 (previously 'recreate required') now receives 3 for recreate and 4 for feature-disabled; testWrongVersions in UpdateCommandDistTest only asserts the error message text and the exit code is never checked, so the renumbering ships completely unverified and old consumers misclassify recreate results as feature-disabled.

[ADVISORY] testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message and never asserts the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4) that UpdateCompatibilityCheck/UpdateCompatibilityMetadata now return via picocli.exit(). If the picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) call is dropped or the constant is renumbered again, the test still passes because it never checks the exit code — the programmatic signal the operator relies on to distinguish 'feature disabled' from other failures is unverified. Checked quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java, the only test file touching these commands in the diff; testCompatible checks exit code 0 but no test checks exit code 4.

[ADVISORY] The diff documents that the Operator 'will fail' when the rolling-updates feature is not enabled (advanced-configuration.adoc CAUTION block) and hard-codes the feature on for every UpgradeTest deployment, but no test in the diff exercises the disabled-feature failure path in the operator. An operator user following the old CR shape (no features.enabled entry) hits the documented hard failure, yet the only integration tests for update strategies all inject Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES into every deployment, so the operator-side enforcement behavior is only verified indirectly through the CLI dist test; a regression that makes the operator silently proceed without the feature would pass the suite. Checked operator/src/test/java/org/keycloak/operator/testsuite/integration/UpgradeTest.java — the sole operator test file changed.

[BUG] RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is silently changed from 4 to 3, breaking every existing consumer that branches on the documented exit code 4 to mean 'recreate upgrade required'. Any operator, CI pipeline, or script written against the prior contract that invoked `kc.sh update-compatibility` and checked exit code 4 to decide 'shut down before applying configuration' now receives 3 with no code change on their side; with picocli conventions, 1 is software error, and 3 is not a documented picocli code, so the change is also read as a generic failure by generic wrappers, and the operator's own decision logic (if it shells out to this command) misclassifies 'recreate required' as an error. Nothing in the diff updates external consumers or the exit-code documentation table other than appending row 4.

[ADVISORY] The update-compatibility tool's entire existing behavior is newly gated behind the `rolling-updates` preview feature, so upgrading Keycloak breaks existing automation until users edit their invocations to pass --features=rolling-updates. Operators with existing scripts/pipelines that call `kc.sh update-compatibility ...` (without the new flag) get exit code 4 and an error after upgrading, a silent contract break during the deploy window: the update check that used to run now fails, and the docs even recommend adding the flag to the template command (docs/guides/templates/kc.adoc), requiring every consumer to update their invocation in lockstep with the upgrade — an expand/contract violation where the old invocation form is removed in the same step that introduces the gate.

[ADVISORY] FEATURE_DISABLED is assigned exit code 4, the exact code that previously (and in already-released versions of this preview tool) meant RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE, so any existing automation that branches on exit code 4 will interpret a disabled-feature failure as 'recreate upgrade required'. Operators running scripts written against the prior release will see exit code 4 from `update-compatibility` and conclude they must shut down the deployment for a recreate upgrade, when the actual cause is only that the preview feature is disabled — a destructive action taken on a misread failure signal; the same scripts will also silently miss genuine recreate-required results, which now exit 3.

[ADVISORY] The feature-disabled path reports the error only via printError and picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED), but the picocli exit-code mechanism only takes effect if the command's execution path actually honors it (CommandLine.execute return value); in the Keycloak Quarkus CLI the run() return is ignored and the process exit is derived elsewhere, so a mismatch would make every disabled-feature invocation exit with the generic error code while the docs promise code 4. Docs (update-compatibility.adoc exit-code table row 4) and the operator, which relies on distinguishing exit codes to decide rolling vs recreate strategy, would misclassify the disabled-feature case; no test in this diff asserts the exit code of the disabled path (testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the message), so a regression here is invisible.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly gates both `update-compatibility` subcommands behind `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)` in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()`, printing an error and exiting with `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` (exit code 4) when not enabled. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] FEATURE_DISABLED is assigned exit code 4, the exact code that previously (and in already-released versions of this preview tool) meant RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE, so any existing automation that branches on exit code 4 will interpret a disabled-feature failure as 'recreate upgrade required'. Operators running scripts written against the prior release will see exit code 4 from `update-compatibility` and conclude they must shut down the deployment for a recreate upgrade, when the actual cause is only that the preview feature is disabled — a destructive action taken on a misread failure signal; the same scripts will also silently miss genuine recreate-required results, which now exit 3.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from `4` to `3` and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (`CompatibilityResult.java`). This is a backward-compatibility/behavior-change concern grounded in the diff, not an internal correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The feature-disabled path reports the error only via printError and picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED), but the picocli exit-code mechanism only takes effect if the command's execution path actually honors it (CommandLine.execute return value); in the Keycloak Quarkus CLI the run() return is ignored and the process exit is derived elsewhere, so a mismatch would make every disabled-feature invocation exit with the generic error code while the docs promise code 4. Docs (update-compatibility.adoc exit-code table row 4) and the operator, which relies on distinguishing exit codes to decide rolling vs recreate strategy, would misclassify the disabled-feature case; no test in this diff asserts the exit code of the disabled path (testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the message), so a regression here is invisible.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new disabled-feature early-exit path in both UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata that calls picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) and returns, and updates docs/exit-code constants to introduce FEATURE_DISABLED=4. However, the new test testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message and does not assert the exit code for this new behavior, so any regression in the disabled-feature exit-code behavior would not be caught by tests. The finding’s broader claim that Keycloak’s CLI ignores picocli.exit and would always return a generic code is not verifiable from the diff alone, but the lack of an exit-code assertion is a concrete, diff-grounded gap.
